top.line: The newsroom's reading meter on a composer's site: sellable units, pathways to a buyer and CC BY with a paid licence.
top.para: Gabriel's site should look like a composer's site, with the newsroom's way to be paid added through api.newsroom.sgit.ai: £5 of starting credit, a few pence a page, a balance that can go negative and Stripe top-ups. Every lesson, score, analysis, how-to and master becomes a sellable unit, pathways lead from a viewer to a buyer, and CC BY with a paid licence lets works travel without selling exclusivity.

in-short.line: Not a newsroom's look; a built meter as an open API; sellable units, pathways and a daily habit.
in-short.para: His market is musicians, producers and students. Works that should travel go out under CC BY with a paid licence alongside.

look.line: A composer's site has a biography, works, clips and news; the newsroom adds a meter, not a look.
look.para: His question after seeing a top-up work was the right one, and the answer is the starter kit's site with the meter added.

meter.line: £5 of credit, pence a page by how much was read, a rating, a negative balance and Stripe top-ups.
meter.para: It runs on this site today and is published as api.newsroom.sgit.ai under Apache 2.0, with the reader's state in the reader's browser on his domain.

plug.line: One element per page, a balance chip, one config and the account pages copied as they are.
plug.para: The kind sets the price class: article, note, issue, collection, page or free. Reading-list links make syllabi; personas for his site would be a small piece of new work.

pathways.line: Found on a platform, a page on his site, more pages, a top-up, then a larger purchase.
pathways.para: The meter covers pages and top-ups today; scores, masters, licences and lessons need payment links of their own.

units.line: Lessons, scores, analyses, how-tos, video breakdowns and masters, each a page that can earn.
units.para: Each is a door for someone who wants to go deeper, and a couple catching on brings traffic to all the others.

market.line: Composers, musicians, producers and students: an advanced readership, and a large one.
market.para: Ideas to try: more starting credit for his students, and fans who enjoy supporting the work.

licences.line: CC BY lets works travel; a paid licence gives other terms, never exclusivity.
licences.para: CC licences are non-exclusive and not revocable, so anything he may sell exclusively stays out of CC BY. If he is an SPA member, he should ask SPA in writing first.

ideas.line: Three prices per work, score previews, series, lesson bundles, commissions, requests and patrons.
ideas.para: Read it, use it under CC BY, or license it with the masters.

habit.line: The workflow is the product: describe it when it happens, and let agents publish it.
habit.para: Traffic comes from publishing a lot; he then learns what gets traction and how to price it.

limits.line: The meter is not yet on his site, earnings are unknown, and the licensing notes are not legal advice.
limits.para: Students' credit, fans' clubs, his personas and larger purchases are proposals.

sources.line: The conversation, api.newsroom.sgit.ai, Creative Commons' FAQ and legal code, SPA's by-laws.
